wallet_deployed_by_factory_done.meaning: BuilderFactory.deployBuilder() has deployed the BuilderWallet and called init(legitimateAdmin) on it
wallet_deployed_by_factory_done.checkpoint: after factory deployBuilder() deployment and init(legitimateAdmin) call, before any attacker init() call

builder_admin_set_before.meaning: builderAdmin is already set on the BuilderWallet before the checked init() call

wallet_token_balance_before.meaning: tokens accumulated in the BuilderWallet (builder fees) before the checked action

reinit_attempted.meaning: an init() call is attempted on the BuilderWallet after builderAdmin is already set

reinit_succeeded.meaning: the init() call on the BuilderWallet completes successfully despite builderAdmin already being set

tokens_stolen.meaning: all tokens accumulated in the BuilderWallet are stolen by an attacker in a single transaction

assumptions: The checked action is a call to BuilderWallet.init() after builderAdmin has already been set by the factory deployment.
The report's impact is potential: the plan encodes the conditional scenario in which an attacker's init() succeeds and sweeps accumulated fees, not an inevitable outcome.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the attacker's init() overwrites an existing builderAdmin or whether the factory's init() had already completed; the exact re-initialization mechanism is not specified.

Report does not specify the exact access-control guard expected (onlyFactory vs constructor-set admin) as a single required property, so the authorization predicate is bound to the report-stated 'builderAdmin already set' condition.

limitations: The impact is potential; the plan formalizes the report-supported conditional scenario rather than asserting theft as certain.
No concrete token balance is given; wallet_token_balance_before is symbolic and only constrained to be positive.
Theft is represented as a grounded Boolean occurrence because the report does not give a numeric transfer relation.
